Contrast is a whole-brain, group-level self vs celebrity task-evoked map in healthy adults assessing self/other social processing; meets global and local social processing criteria.

Task is trait-based self vs celebrity judgments, not a social communication task (faces, emotion, gaze, etc.); local inclusion criteria SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/I2 not met. Global criteria are met.
Self- vs celebrity judgment directly measures perception/understanding of self (self-judgment contrast) in a whole-brain group map of healthy adults.

Friend vs celebrity is a whole-brain, group-level social task contrast in healthy adults assessing social processing of others; meets global and local social processing criteria.

Friend vs celebrity contrast measures others (close other) not self; local inclusion PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/I2 not met. Global criteria are met.
Friend vs celebrity directly measures perception/understanding of others (close other vs non-close), is whole-brain and group-level in healthy adults.
Whole-brain interaction/regression identifies brain regions in the self vs celebrity contrast in healthy adults; it assesses social processing and meets global and local social processing criteria.
This analysis concerns self vs celebrity and the modulation by interdependence; it does not target affiliation/attachment contrasts (AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2 not met). Global criteria are met.
Analysis examines self-referential processing modulation, not social communication (faces, gaze, emotion); SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/I2 not met. Global criteria are met.
Analysis identifies modulation of self- vs celebrity neural responses (self-judgment), which maps onto Perception/Understanding of Self; whole-brain group-level in healthy adults.
This analysis is focused on self-related contrast (self vs celebrity); it does not measure perception/understanding of others (PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2 not met). Global criteria are met.
Whole-brain regression of friend vs celebrity contrast in healthy adults assessing social processing of others; meets global and local social processing criteria.
Friend vs celebrity (close other vs non-close) is consistent with affiliation/attachment constructs (close relationship processing); whole-brain group-level regression in healthy adults.

Friend vs celebrity contrast measures others, not self; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/I2 not met. Global criteria are met.

Contrast compares partnered vs non-partnered joint-action (haptic coupling) and explicitly reports social-cognitive (mPFC, TPJ, pSTS) and somatosensory networks; meets global healthy adult whole-brain criteria and measures social processing.

This analysis contrasts partnered versus non-partnered movement but does not assay affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., loved one vs stranger, bonding measures). Missing local inclusion criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2.

Partnered conditions involve exchange of haptic cues (receptive and productive aspects of communication); analysis shows areas (pSTS, TPJ, somatosensory) consistent with social communication. Global and local criteria met.
The partnered > non-partnered contrast is not a task explicitly probing self-judgment, agency, or self-knowledge as defined by PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/I2; those local inclusion criteria are not met.
Partnered > non-partnered contrast engages mentalizing and social-perception regions (TPJ, mPFC, pSTS), directly measuring perception/understanding of others. Meets global and local criteria.

Leading is a social role in joint action (leader/follower dynamics); the contrast isolates leading-related activations within the partnered context and reports social-cognitive/motor areas—meets global and local inclusion criteria.
The Leading > conjunction contrast does not probe affiliation/attachment constructs (no measures of bonding/cooperation vs competition or loved one vs stranger). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2.

Leading involves signaling movement intentions via haptic channels (productive social communication); the contrast targets leader-specific activations consistent with communicative signaling—meets local criteria for social communication.

Leading contrasts emphasize self-initiation, motor planning, and agency-related processes (self-oriented action); this meets the PERCEPTION_SELF criteria (agency/self-related processing) along with global criteria.

The Leading > conjunction contrast focuses on self-initiated motor/planning processes rather than explicit perception/understanding of others (Theory-of-Mind/empathy); PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2 are not the primary target here.

Following is an explicitly social task (responding to partner's haptic cues); the contrast isolates follower-related activations including social-perceptual regions, meeting global and local criteria.
The Following > conjunction contrast does not measure affiliation/attachment per se (no bonding or relationship-scale measures); missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2.

Following entails reception of haptic cues and tracking partner motion (receptive social communication); reported activations (pSTS, MT+/V5, S2) fit Social Communication criteria. Global and local criteria satisfied.
Following is externally-driven and the contrast targets sensory/perceptual processing of partner cues rather than explicit self-perception or agency judgments; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/I2 are not met.

Following explicitly requires perceiving and tracking the partner's actions; the contrast activates regions (pSTS, TPJ/mentalizing areas) tied to perception/understanding of others, meeting global and local criteria.
Mutual is an explicitly social, symmetric partnered interaction and the contrast reveals mentalizing and reward networks; global and local social-processing criteria are met.
Although Mutual is cooperative, the analysis does not probe affiliation/attachment scales or bonding contrasts (e.g., loved one vs stranger); missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2.

Mutual interaction involves bidirectional haptic exchange and joint coordination (productive and receptive communication), and the contrast engages communicative/social-perceptual regions; local criteria satisfied.
Mutual > conjunction emphasizes mutual/mentalizing and reward networks rather than explicit self-judgment or agency tasks; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/I2 are not met.
Mutual engages mentalizing and social-reward circuits (mPFC, TPJ, PCC) which index perception/understanding of others; meets global and local inclusion criteria.

The improvisation contrast (Leading + Solo > Mutual + Alone) is designed to isolate motor-planning and working-memory processes of improvisation and includes non-partnered (non-social) conditions; it does not specifically measure social processing as required by SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I1/I2.
Improvisation contrast does not assess affiliation/attachment constructs or bonding measures; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2.

This contrast targets improvisational generation and distinguishes generation vs movement variability; it is not primarily an analysis of social communication reception/production (SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/I2 not met).

Although improvisation involves self-generated movement, this contrast isolates motor-generation and working-memory processes rather than explicit self-judgment/agency tasks as defined by PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/I2.
The improvisation contrast includes non-partnered conditions and is focused on generation/variability of movement, not on perceiving or reasoning about others (PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2 not met).

The self-initiation versus externally-triggered contrast ([Leading + Solo + Mutual + Alone] > Following) explicitly probes self- vs other-driven actions within the joint-action paradigm and includes partnered conditions; it therefore pertains to social processing in the context of interpersonal roles and meets global and local social-processing criteria.
This analysis contrasts self-initiated vs externally-triggered movement and does not probe affiliation/attachment constructs or bonding measures; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2.

Self-initiation vs externally-triggered movement in a partnered context taps into signaling and perceiving partner cues (productive/receptive social exchanges); meets SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION local criteria as well as global criteria.
This contrast directly isolates self-initiated versus externally-triggered actions (agency/self-initiation), matching PERCEPTION_SELF inclusion criteria and global criteria.

Although this contrast contrasts self- and externally-driven actions, its primary focus is on self-initiation (agency) rather than explicitly measuring perception/understanding of others (PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2 not the main target).

Joint improvisation (interaction with a partner during improvisation) is an explicitly social joint-action task; the analysis concerns interpersonal coordination and thus meets social-processing local and global criteria.
The joint improvisation analysis does not assess affiliation/attachment constructs or bonding measures (AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2 absent).
Joint improvisation entails bidirectional haptic signaling and coordination (production and reception of social cues); this meets SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION local criteria together with global criteria.
Joint improvisation requires self-generated action and agency (leaders producing movements within a dyadic context); this matches PERCEPTION_SELF inclusion criteria along with global criteria.

Joint improvisation necessarily involves perceiving and responding to a partner's actions and intentions (mentalizing/action-perception), meeting PERCEPTION_OTHERS local and global inclusion criteria.

The contrast does not involve self-referential judgments or self-related processing. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Affectivity>cooperativity directly probes understanding others' affective/mental states (theory of mind/empathy-related processing) in a whole-brain group contrast with healthy adults, meeting global and local criteria.

The analysis is a group-level whole-brain contrast of Pain > Neutral in a task that manipulates perspective-taking (Self, Loved-one, Stranger) and probes empathy for others' pain, which is a social processing task. Global criteria for healthy adult sample and whole-brain group-level task-evoked map are met, and the contrast measures social processing.

This specific analysis is the main effect of pain irrespective of perspective (Pain > Neutral) and does not specifically test affiliation/attachment contrasts such as Loved-one vs Stranger, so local inclusion criteria are not met (task does involve relationships, but this particular contrast does not isolate affiliation/attachment). Missing inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1, AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

The analysis uses animated hands/feet depicting pain and is not a social communication task (e.g., faces, gaze, facial expression recognition) and the contrast is Pain > Neutral across perspectives; thus it does not meet SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 or SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.

Although the study includes Self perspective conditions, this specific analysis is the overall Pain > Neutral main effect across all perspectives and does not isolate self-related processing (e.g., Self > Other). Therefore it does not meet PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 or PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

The task involves empathy (which can index perception of others), but this particular contrast is the main effect of pain across all perspectives rather than an Other-specific contrast (e.g., Loved-one or Stranger > Neutral or Self vs Other). Thus it does not satisfy PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 or PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 for this analysis.
